semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {وَمَا خَلَقَ}: «ما» may be in the sense of «مَنْ» (who), and this is the view of a group whose mention preceded in the previous sūra. It was also said: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). Al-Zamakhsharī said: «[i.e.] and by the Powerful One, of mighty power, Who was able to create the male and the female from a single fluid.» I say: the establishment of this view of his, what was objected against it and what was answered on its behalf have already been given in the previous sūra. Abū al-Dardāʾ read «والذَّكرِ والأنثى», and ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «والذي خَلَق»; and al-Kisāʾī — and Thaʿlab transmitted it from some of the early generations (salaf) — [read] «وما خَلَقَ الذَّكَرِ» with «الذكَرِ» in the genitive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «As a badal (substitute) for the position of "ما خَلَقَ" in the sense of "وما خَلَقَه", i.e. and by what Allah created, the male; and implying "الله" was permissible because it is known that He alone creates.» The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: «It may also be explained as [conjoined on] an imagined verbal noun, i.e. "and by the creation of the male", as in his saying:
4583 - تَطُوفُ العُفاةُ بأبوابِه ... كما طاف بالبَيْعَةِ الراهبِ
(Those seeking favours circle around his doors, as the monk circles around the church.)
with "الراهب" in the genitive on the supposition of the verbal noun having been pronounced, i.e. "like the circling of the monk".» End of quotation. What appears [to me] in explaining the verse [of poetry] is that its origin is «الراهبيّ» with the yāʾ of relation (nisba), relating to the attribute, then it was lightened; and this is rare, like their saying أَحْمري and دَوَّاري. This very explanation [applies] to the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
4584 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فَقِلْ في مَقيلٍ نَحْسُه مُتَغَيِّبِ
(…so take your midday rest in a resting-place whose ill omen is absent.)
which the Kufans cited as evidence for putting the fāʿil (agent) first. The majority read {تجلى} as a past verb, its fāʿil being a pronoun referring to the day. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr [read] «تتجلى» with two tāʾs, i.e. the sun. And «تُجْلي» was read, with ḍamma on the tāʾ and sukūn on the jīm, i.e. also the sun; and there must be an omitted [pronoun] referring back to the day, i.e. "it [the sun] becomes manifest — or reveals [things] — in it".

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ}: This is the apodosis (jawāb) of the oath. It is also possible that it [the apodosis] is omitted, as was said regarding its parallels mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {أعطى}: He omitted the two objects of «أعطى», the object of «اتقى», and the object of «صَدَّقَ» [which would be] in the genitive with «على», because the purpose is the mention of these events without their attached elements (mutaʿallaqāt); likewise the attached elements of the stinginess and the self-sufficiency. And His saying: {فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ للعسرى} is either by way of correspondence (muqābala) with His saying: {فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لليسرى}, or because «نيسِّره» means "We prepare him", and preparing can be for ease and for hardship.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {وَمَا يُغْنِي}: «ما» may be negative, or a denying (inkārī) interrogative.
His saying: {تردى}: either from destruction, or from تردّى بأكفانِه (he wrapped himself in his shrouds), which is a metonymy for death, as in his saying:
4585 - وخُطَّا بأَطْرافِ الأسِنَّةِ مَضْجَعي ... ورُدَّا على عَيْنَيَّ فَضْلَ رِدائيا
(Mark out my resting-place with the tips of the spearheads, and draw the rest of my cloak back over my eyes.)
and the saying of another:
4586 - نَصيبُك مِمَّا تَجْمَعُ الدهرَ كلَّه ... رِداءان تلوى فيهما وحَنُوطُ
(Your share of all that you gather throughout time is two cloaks in which you are wrapped, and embalming spices.)

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {نَاراً تلظى}: It has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara that al-Bazzī doubles the tāʾ, and the doubling here is difficult because of the meeting of two sākin letters in it, not within the permitted limit; it is the counterpart of His saying {إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ} [al-Nūr: 15], which has already been given. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is read with kasra on the tanwīn and doubled tāʾ, and its explanation was mentioned at {وَلاَ تَيَمَّمُواْ الخبيث} [al-Baqara: 267]." End of quotation. This is an odd reading, but it accords with analogy in that two sākin letters do not meet in it. As for his saying "its explanation was mentioned": what he said in al-Baqara is of no use at all here. For he said there: "It is read with a doubled tāʾ preceded by an alif, which is a combination of two sākin letters, and what made that permissible is the lengthening that is in the alif."

Ibn al-Zubayr, Sufyān, Zayd b. ʿAlī and Ṭalḥa read «تتلظى» with two tāʾs, which is the original form.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ الأشقى}: It was said: «الأشقى» and «الأَتْقى» mean «الشقيّ» and «التقيّ» ("the wretched" and "the pious"), with no comparative sense in them, because the Fire is not restricted to the most wretched, and avoiding it is not restricted to the most pious. It was also said: rather they are in their normal sense, which is the view of al-Zamakhsharī. He said: "If you say: how did He say «لا يَصْلاها إلاَّ الأشقى» {وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الأتقى}, when it is known that every wretched person will burn in it and every pious person will be kept away from it, and that burning is not restricted to the most wretched of the wretched, nor salvation to the most pious of the pious? And if you claim that He made «النار» indefinite so as to mean a particular Fire restricted to the most wretched, what will you do with His saying {وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الأتقى}? For it is known that even the most iniquitous of the Muslims is kept away from that particular Fire, not only the most pious of them. I say: the verse comes in the weighing of the two states of a great one among the polytheists and a great one among the believers. So it was intended to be emphatic in describing their two opposite qualities. So it said «الأشقى» and made it restricted to the burning, as though the Fire had been created only for him; and it said «الأتقى» and made it restricted to the salvation, as though Paradise had been created only for him. It was also said: they are Abū Jahl or Umayya b. Khalaf, and Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him." End of quotation. So his answer comes down to the two being specific individuals.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {يتزكى}: The majority read {يتزكى}, the imperfect of «تَزَكَّى». Al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī, the Commander of the Faithful, read «يزكى», assimilating the tāʾ into the zāy. There are two views on this clause. One: that it is in the position of ḥāl from the agent of «يُؤْتي», i.e. "he gives it, purifying himself by it." The second: that it has no grammatical position, on the basis that it is a badal (substitute) for the ṣila of «الذي». Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned both, and the Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] judged it to be forced.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {تجزى}: It is an adjective of «نعمة», i.e. "that is repaid to the human being." It was brought as a passive imperfect only for the sake of the verse-endings, since the original would be «يُجْزيها إياه» or «يُجْزِيه إياها».

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ ابتغآء}: There are two views on its accusative. One: that it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be a mafʿūl lahu in meaning, because the meaning is: he gives his wealth only seeking the face of his Lord, not to repay a favour." He took this from the saying of al-Farrāʾ, who said: "It is put in the accusative on the interpretation: «ما أعْطَيْتُك ابتغاءَ جزائِك، بل ابتغاءَ وجهِ اللَّهِ تعالى» ('I did not give to you seeking your recompense, but seeking the face of Allah the Exalted')." The second: that it is accusative as a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), since it does not fall under the genus of «مِنْ نعمة». This is the reading of the majority, I mean the accusative with the lengthened alif.

Yaḥyā read it in the nominative, lengthened, as a badal (substitute) for the position of «مِنْ نعمة», because the position of that is nominative: either as agent or as mubtadaʾ, and «مِنْ» is redundant (mazīda) in both cases. The badal is the dialect of Tamīm, because they treat a discontinuous exception in a non-affirmative context like a continuous one. Al-Zamakhsharī cited for both the accusative and the badal the saying of Bishr b. Abī Khāzim:

[Translator's note: the verse numbers are garbled in the source, printed as «458 - 7-» and «458 - 8-»; from the sequence they should be 4587 and 4588.]

4587 - أَضْحَتْ خَلاءً قِفاراً أَنيسَ بها ... إلاَّ الجآذِرُ والظِّلْمانَُِ تَخْتَلِفُ
(It has become empty and desolate, with no companion in it except the gazelle fawns and the ostriches, which come and go)

and the saying of another, for the nominative:

4588 - وبَلْدَةٍ ليس بها أنيسُ ... إلاَّ اليَعافيرُ وإلاَّ العِيْسُ
(And a land with no companion in it, except the gazelles and the pale camels)

Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ permitted the nominative in «ابتغاء» as a badal for the position of «نِعْمَةٍ», but that is remote." I say: it is as though he had not come across it as a reading; his calling it remote is itself remote, since it is a widespread dialect. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ابْتِغا» shortened.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {وَلَسَوْفَ يرضى}: This is the answer to an implied oath. The majority read «يرضى» as active. It was also read as passive, from «أَرْضاه الله», which is close to His saying at the end of Sūrat Ṭā Hā {لَعَلَّكَ ترضى} and {ترضى} [Ṭā Hā: 130].
